Luaba had been on a mission to find delegates for a peace conference at the time that he was kidnapped; officials stated that he had approached a local chief to invite him to attend the conference and was taken hostage instead. At least 196 people, including five assailants, were killed across three of the assaults, while 111 people were injured across all four events. The ensuing clashes lasted until December 18, 2018. In addition, several of the victims were behaded or sexually assaulted; it is unknown if any hostages were taken and held by the assailants beyond 24 hours. No group claimed responsibility; however, sources attributed the attacks to Batende tribal members and posited that the incidents were related to conflicts over resources and monthly tribal duties.
motive: The specific motive is unknown; however, sources posited that the attack was related to conflicts over resources and monthly tribal duties.
weapdetail: Assault rifles, hunting rifles, gasoline, machetes, and bows and arrows were used in the attack.
propcomment: Sources estimated that 1,000 building were damaged, including houses, churches, schools, and health centers, across incidents 201812160027, 201812160028, 201812160029, and 201812160030.
addnotes: There is doubt that this incident meets terrorism-related criteria. A source suspected that elements of the military may have taken part in the inident. Another source stated that the attack "had support from local authorities and elements within the security forces." Casualty numbers represent a division of the total number of those killed across incidents 201812160028, 201812160029, and 201812160030 and those wounded across incidents 201812160027, 201812160028, 201812160029, and 201812160030.
scite1: "Revealed: DR Congo’s ‘invisible’ massacre," Daily Times, February 9, 2019.

At least 57 students escaped shortly after the abduction. Another hostage escaped on May 17, 2016, along with her infant who was born in captivity. The victim noted that six captives had been killed. An additional 21 hostages were released on October 13, 2016, along with a child who was born in captivity. On November 5, 2016, another hostage was rescued along with her child. Another hostage was released on January 5, 2017, along with her child who was born in captivity. After negotiations with the government, 82 hostages were released on May 6, 2017. summary: 06/00/2018: Sometime between April 1 and August 31, 2018, assailants raided Namutina, Tambura, South Sudan. This was one of at least 30 attacks between April and August, 2018 in which 887 people were abducted. At least 128 hostages were released as of February 4, 2020 while the fate of the remaining victims is unknown. No group claimed responsibility for the incident; however, sources attributed the attack to the Sudan People's Liberation Movement in Opposition (SPLM-IO), noting that many of the female victims were sexually assaulted and were forced to marry members of the group, while many male victims were forced into becoming fighters for the group.

motive: The specific motive is unknown; however, sources stated that many of the female victims were sexually assaulted and/or enslaved, while many of the male victims were forcibly recruited to become members of the Sudan People's Liberation Movement in Opposition (SPLM-IO).
weapdetail: AK-47 assault rifles, machetes, clubs, whips, gun butts, and sharpened sticks were used in the attack.
